{{Short description|Italian mathematician (born 1980)}}
[[File:Corinna Ulcigrai on Chaotic Properties of Area Preserving Flows in 2019.jpg|thumb|Ulcigrai lectures in 2019]]
'''Corinna Ulcigrai''' (born 3 January 1980, [[Trieste]])<ref name="plus"/> is an Italian [[mathematician]] working on [[dynamical system]]s.<ref name="ewm">{{citation|url=http://www.europeanwomeninmaths.org/women-in-math/portrait/corinna-ulcigrai|title=Corinna Ulcigrai|department=Women in Math|journal=EWM Newsletter|publisher=European Women in Mathematics|date=6 November 2012|volume=21|access-date=15 May 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180115112105/http://www.europeanwomeninmaths.org/women-in-math/portrait/corinna-ulcigrai|archive-date=15 January 2018|url-status=dead}}</ref> With Krzysztof Frączek in 2013, Ulcigrai is known for proving that in the [[Ehrenfest model]] (a mathematical abstraction of billiards with an infinite array of rectangular obstacles, used to model gas diffusion) most trajectories are not [[ergodic]].<ref name="plus">{{citation|url=https://plus.maths.org/content/chaos-billiard-table|title=Chaos on the billiard table|journal=+Plus Magazine|first=Marianne|last=Freiberger|date=8 May 2014}}</ref>

==Education and career==
Ulcigrai obtained her Ph.D. in 2007 from [[Princeton University]] with [[Yakov Sinai]] as her thesis advisor.<ref name="ewm"/><ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=174125}}</ref> She has worked at the [[University of Bristol]], [[United Kingdom]].<ref name="bristol-whitehead"/> and is currently a professor at the [[University of Zurich]], [[Switzerland]].

==Recognition==
Ulcigrai was awarded the [[European Mathematical Society#Prizes|European Mathematical Society Prize]] in 2012,<ref name="ewm"/><ref>{{citation|url=http://www.euro-math-soc.eu/prizes-awarded-6th-european-congress-mathematics-krakow-0|title=Prizes awarded at the 6th European Congress of Mathematics in Krakow|date=2 July 2012|work=Press release|publisher=European Mathematical Society|access-date=15 May 2015|archive-date=30 June 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150630170129/http://www.euro-math-soc.eu/prizes-awarded-6th-european-congress-mathematics-krakow-0|url-status=dead}}</ref> and the [[Whitehead Prize]] in 2013.<ref name="bristol-whitehead">{{citation|url=http://www.bristol.ac.uk/maths/news/2013/corinna-ulcighrai-prize.html|title=Corinna Ulcigrai awarded prestigious Whitehead Prize by the London Mathematical Society|date=9 July 2013|publisher=Bristol University School of Mathematics|access-date=15 May 2015|archive-date=16 August 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160816080359/http://www.bristol.ac.uk/maths/news/2013/corinna-ulcighrai-prize.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>

In 2020, Ulcigrai was the winner of the [[Michael Brin Prize in Dynamical Systems]], "for her fundamental work on the ergodic theory of locally Hamiltonian flows on surfaces, of translation flows on periodic surfaces and wind-tree models, and her seminal work on higher genus generalizations of Markov and Lagrange spectra".<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.ams.org/journals/notices/202007/rnoti-p1051.pdf|journal=Notices of the American Mathematical Society|department=Mathematics People|title=Ulcigrai Awarded Brin Prize|first=Giovanni|last=Forni|page=1051|date=August 2020|volume=67|issue=7}}</ref>
